front.title: Protected Delegated Transaction Authority: Exact-Effect Reconstruction, Non-Bearer Authorization, and Execution-Finality Enforcement

abstract.t: A cryptographically valid signature, an authenticated request, a delegated credential or a previously approved operation does not necessarily establish authorization for the exact consequential operation about to take effect. This document describes an informational security architecture for delegated digital operations in which authority is bound at collection time in one protected enforcement domain, the actual execution-facing operation is reconstructed in a second, and a protected Finality Sink decides whether that exact effect may be released. It covers exclusive signing, non-bearer sink-bound execution handles, final native byte reconstruction, delegated-code and account-abstraction cases such as EIP-7702, atomic budget consumption, crash recovery with explicit unknown outcomes, effect-path coverage, and financial profiles for payments, cards, tokenized assets, stablecoins, offline money and cross-chain transfers. Enforcement claims are limited to effect paths actually under control.
